posts.title: Watched: The End of Oak Street
posts.description: David Robert Mitchell · 2026 · 4/5 Excellent movie. Very weird, in a good way in various places. Some parts were expected but still overall a lot of fun. I enjoyed how the men in the movie were mostly helpless. Because the film has a slow ramp, I got this weird feeling that the characters were headed toward doom and they didn’t even know it. Sort of like when you drive the opposite way of traffic

posts.title: Read: Theo of Golden
posts.description: Allen Levi · 2023 · 5/5 Great book. A little slow to get going. Reads at first a bit like The Correspondent by Virginia Evans, which in itself is a fantastic book. But as the story builds, it takes many turns.

posts.title: AI Doesn't Take Over. We Give It the Keys.
posts.description: A company gives AI access to its source code because its engineers ship faster. Then production systems, because it handles outages better. Then purchasing, because it negotiates better deals. Then budgeting, because its forecasts improve. Each success earns another set of keys.
